# spec-kitty-design — LLM Deep Context Bundle

This is the deep-context companion to `llms.txt`. It packs everything an LLM
needs to reason about the Spec Kitty design system in a single read: the
mission, the architecture decisions, the full token catalogue, the component
manifest, the quality gates, and the recipe for adding new pieces. Code is the
source of truth; this file mirrors what is in the repo at the time of writing.

---

## 1. Project overview

`spec-kitty-design` is a token-driven, **elements-first** web design system for
the Spec Kitty / Priivacy-ai ecosystem. A single CSS-custom-property token file
(`@spec-kitty/tokens`) is the authoritative source for every visual value.

The component layer is a **custom element** (ADR-8): behaviour lives in a Lit
element in `@spec-kitty/elements`, its CSS source of record lives in
`@spec-kitty/styles`, and framework packages are **generated from the Custom
Elements Manifest** rather than hand-maintained. `@spec-kitty/react` is the first
and currently only such package, and every file in it is generated.

This replaced a three-package topology in which `@spec-kitty/angular` held
hand-written Angular wrappers. That package was deleted in #102 and Angular is
not a target of this repo; references to it in older material are history.

The system is published interactively as a Storybook catalogue and as two static
demo pages (`blog-demo.html`, `dashboard-demo.html`), deployed to GitHub Pages.

### Repository layout

```
spec-kitty-design/
  packages/
    tokens/         # @spec-kitty/tokens — CSS custom properties + Falling Sky / Swansea / JetBrains Mono
    styles/         # @spec-kitty/styles — the CSS source of record, plus GENERATED static HTML
    elements/       # @spec-kitty/elements — the Lit custom elements, and the AUTHORED markup module
    react/          # @spec-kitty/react — GENERATED React wrappers. Never hand-edited; CI fails on drift.
  fixtures/
    elements-behaviour/  # the behaviour suite's subjects
    react-consumer/      # proves the wrappers work in a real React render
    vite-consumer/       # proves the package resolves through a real bundler
  apps/
    storybook/      # Storybook 10.x catalogue (web-components renderer, ADR-13)
    demo/           # Static blog-demo.html, dashboard-demo.html, index.html
  docs/
    architecture/
      decisions/    # ADRs (ADR-1 through ADR-13 + ADR-3 addendum)
      research/
      validation/
      assets/
  behaviours.json        # the behaviour id registry (ADR-11) — 15 ids, 14 applicable
  mutations.json         # one red-first mutation per (behaviour, subject) pair
  expected-parts.json    # shrink-only ::part() ratchet
  expected-docs.json     # exact-equality ratchet on documented attributes and methods
  suite-budget.json      # the two CI time ceilings, with their measurements
  doctrine/         # Org-layer doctrine bundle (brand voice, visual identity, directives)
  kitty-specs/      # Mission specifications under spec-kitty governance
  .kittify/         # Spec Kitty runtime config and skills
  .github/workflows # CI: ci-quality.yml, pr-preview.yml, release.yml, storybook-deploy.yml
  scripts/          # the generators and the gates — see §"Gates" below
```

### Deployed surfaces

- Storybook: <https://stijn-dejongh.github.io/spec-kitty-design/>
- Blog demo: <https://stijn-dejongh.github.io/spec-kitty-design/blog-demo.html>
- Dashboard demo: <https://stijn-dejongh.github.io/spec-kitty-design/dashboard-demo.html>

### Authoritative agent guide

`CLAUDE.md` at the repo root is the canonical entry point for AI agents. It
points at the ADRs (ADR-001 token-only CSS, ADR-002 dependency direction,
ADR-003 token schema), the doctrine bundle, and the linting / commit rules. If
this file and `CLAUDE.md` disagree, `CLAUDE.md` wins.

---

## 2. Architecture (ADR summary)

> **Reading order.** ADR-1 through ADR-7 are the original design and are
> summarised as written, so they name Angular where the decision named it.
> ADR-8 through ADR-13 are the elements-first architecture and are what the repo
> does today. Where they disagree, the later ADR wins, and the summaries below
> say so at the point of disagreement. **Nothing in this repo targets Angular:**
> `packages/angular` was deleted in #102 and there is no Angular dependency in
> any `package.json`.

ADRs live under `docs/architecture/decisions/`. Status of every ADR below is
**Accepted**. Each summary captures the canonical decision and its rationale.

### ADR-1 — Token Distribution Format: CSS Custom Properties

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-05-01-1-token-distribution-format.md`.
**Decision:** all design tokens are distributed as `--sk-*` CSS custom
properties on `:root` in a single CSS file; not Tailwind utilities, not a
shadcn-style copy-paste model. **Why:** the static-HTML / Jekyll / Hugo
consumer path requires zero build step, and CSS custom properties are the only
mechanism that lets a single source of truth reach Angular, plain HTML, and
future framework targets identically without per-framework value translation.
Tailwind was rejected because it forces a build step on consumers; shadcn was
rejected because copy-paste structurally guarantees brand drift across consumer
repos.

### ADR-2 — Monorepo Package Topology

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-05-01-2-monorepo-package-topology.md`.
**Decision:** independently publishable packages in a single Nx monorepo, with
a strictly one-directional dependency graph. As shipped today that is
`tokens ← styles ← elements ← react`, with fixtures allowed to depend on any of
them; the ADR states the rule, and ADR-8 changed which packages it applies to.
No framework package may depend on another framework package. **Why:** an
Angular consumer should not pay for HTML/JS bytes and vice-versa; an Angular
LTS major bump should not force a version bump on `@spec-kitty/tokens`; new
framework targets (Vue, Svelte, React) must be additive without restructuring
existing packages. The boundary is enforced by `eslint.config.mjs`'s
`@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` rule.

### ADR-3 — Token Schema and Naming Convention

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-05-01-3-token-schema-naming-convention.md`.
**Decision:** category-prefixed semantic namespace under the `--sk-` product
prefix (pattern `--sk-<category>[-<modifier>[-<variant>]]`), with thirteen
defined categories: `color`, `surface`, `on`, `bg`, `fg`, `border`, `font`,
`text`, `weight`, `space`, `radius`, `shadow`, `motion`. **Why:** flat names
become unmaintainable past ~30 tokens and cannot be linted categorically;
shadcn-style unprefixed names collide with consumer projects. **Critical
rule — semantic pairing:** every surface token has a paired foreground token
(`--sk-surface-<name>` ↔ `--sk-fg-on-<name>` or `--sk-on-tint-<name>`). Mixing
across pairs breaks WCAG contrast guarantees; agents must use paired tokens
together.

### ADR-3 addendum — Token Value Reconciliation (FR-034 satisfied)

`docs/architecture/decisions/ADR-003-addendum-token-values.md`. Records that
the implemented `tokens.css` was reconciled against the Claude Design reference
file (`tmp/Spec Kitty Design System(1)/colors_and_type.css`). Hex was selected
as the canonical color format (not OKLCH) for portability and contributor
familiarity. The generated catalogue `packages/tokens/dist/token-catalogue.json`
contains 98 tokens across 13 categories and is the source for the Stylelint
allowlist. Intentional exclusions: `@font-face` declarations belong in WP02,
not the token layer; `--sk-link` and similar component-scoped aliases stay out.

### ADR-4 — Org-Layer Doctrine Distribution

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-05-01-4-org-layer-doctrine-distribution.md`.
**Decision:** `spec-kitty-design` ships a `doctrine/` directory at repo root,
structured to mirror spec-kitty's `src/doctrine/*/shipped/` layout, ready to be
fetched by `spec-kitty doctrine fetch` once spec-kitty issue #832 lands. It
includes directives `SK-D01` (token authority — all CSS uses `--sk-*` only) and
`SK-D02` (illustration content boundary — mascot/cartoon assets stay out of
software packages), plus `sk-brand-voice` and `sk-visual-identity` styleguides.
**Why:** brand governance must reach every Priivacy-ai project without
per-project copy-paste; an org layer is the single source of truth.

### ADR-5 — npm Supply Chain Security Posture

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-05-01-5-npm-supply-chain-security-posture.md`.
**Decision:** explicit accepted-risk register plus hard CI gates that match or
exceed the spec-kitty Python baseline. Hard gates: `npm audit --audit-level=high`
(FR-041), `npm ci` only (no `npm install`) and lockfile drift check (FR-042),
ESLint security plugin + Semgrep JS (extended FR-018), `npm ci --ignore-scripts`
with documented allowlist (FR-046), all GitHub Actions pinned to immutable SHAs
(FR-043), no `*` or `latest` versions in any `package.json` (C-009). Release-time:
`npm publish --provenance` (FR-044), CycloneDX SBOM (FR-045), 2FA on the
`@spec-kitty` npm scope. **Why:** npm has ~2.4 M packages, no publication
review, and lifecycle hooks that execute at install time — a materially higher
risk surface than PyPI.

### ADR-6 — Storybook Multi-Framework Rendering Strategy

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-05-01-6-storybook-multi-framework-rendering.md`.
**Decision:** WP04 implementer attempts same-story multi-framework rendering
(Option A — Angular and HTML in one story) first; if Storybook's framework
model does not support it without custom plugins, the fallback (Option B —
separate story files per framework with naming convention
`<Category>/<ComponentName> (Angular)` and `<Category>/<ComponentName> (HTML)`)
is pre-authorised, no further approval needed. The shipped catalogue uses
Option B. **Why:** FR-007 single-story-entry requirement must not block the
WP04 timeline if the underlying Storybook API does not cooperate.

### ADR-7 — Storybook 10.x Adoption (Angular 21 Compatibility)

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-05-01-7-storybook-version-10x-adoption.md`.
**Decision:** Storybook 10.x replaces the plan-specified 8.x because
`@storybook/angular@8.x` peer-requires `@angular/core ^19.0.0` and the workspace
is Angular 21.2.11. Storybook 10.x builds in ~10 s, well under the NFR-003
3-minute budget. **Why:** Angular 21 compatibility was the binding constraint;
ADR-006 already pre-authorised version adaptation. Notable 10.x differences
versus 8.x: `addon-essentials` is merged into core, `docs.autodocs` was removed,
`@storybook/blocks` moved to `@storybook/addon-docs/blocks`.

> **ADR-6 and ADR-7 are superseded on the framework question.** Both reason about
> rendering Angular stories. `packages/angular` was deleted in #102 and ADR-13
> replaced the renderer with `@storybook/web-components`. They are summarised
> above as the record of why the catalogue looks as it does, not as current
> guidance.

### ADR-8 — Custom Elements as the Base Layer

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-09-02-8-custom-elements-base-layer.md`.
**Decision:** custom elements (Lit) are the shared base; framework packages
become **thin wrappers generated from the Custom Elements Manifest**. A wrapper
is published only when a consumer exists — frameworks with native custom-element
support (Svelte, Vue, Solid, vanilla) get no package at all, because the manifest
already gives them editor completion and type checking. React leads, because it
had the one identified consumer waiting.

**Two confirmations, in sequence.** #1: one component ships from a single CSS
source and a single manifest into three consumption paths — a bundler-free HTML
page, a Svelte app, and Storybook — **with no wrapper package in existence**.
#2: a generated React wrapper of that same component passes the conformance
matrix without hand editing, and CI fails if the output drifts. #75 discharged
#2, which is why `packages/react` exists; #1 was not invalidated by it.

### ADR-9 — Shadow DOM and the Styling API

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-09-02-9-shadow-dom-and-styling-api.md`.
**Decision:** open shadow roots, and a consumer restyles through `::part()` —
never by reaching into internals. Every declared part must be present and
targetable. **Consequence that bites:** a selector whose leftmost compound
targets an ancestor outside the shadow root is **inert** once the sheet is
adopted, with no error and no warning.
`scripts/check-adopted-css-boundaries.mjs` refuses those, and it is stricter
than the ADR's own four-token enumeration because that enumeration catches only
half of the defect that motivated it.

### ADR-10 — Distribution and Canonical Markup

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-09-02-10-distribution-and-canonical-markup.md`.
**§1** CSS reaches the element as a constructed stylesheet, never a `<style>`
tag, so a consumer CSP without `style-src` cannot strip it.
**§2** every element must reach **both** distribution entries — the ESM
`index.ts` and the IIFE `elements.ts`; `check-elements-entries.mjs` enforces it,
parsed from esbuild's metafile rather than matched as text.
**§3** the element's template is the **sole authored source**: the static HTML
and the styles-layer module are generated from it and CI fails on drift.
**§5** registration goes through a guarded `define()` that warns and no-ops on a
duplicate tag rather than throwing.

### ADR-11 — Verification Stack and Wrapper Generation

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-09-02-11-verification-stack-and-wrapper-generation.md`.
**Decision:** a named list of required behaviours, each with a test and a
**red-first mutation** proving that test detects its own violation.
`behaviours.json` is the registry, `mutations.json` the proofs, and
`scripts/suite-selftest.mjs` runs one full suite per mutation and fails if any
does not produce its named red.

Item 9, **generation determinism**, is a Node-lane obligation: regenerating
wrappers from an unchanged manifest is a no-op, and drift fails CI. It is
declared in `behaviours.json` as SC-023 with `applicable: false`, because
`build-react-wrappers.mjs --check` discharges it — the harness is browser-only
and has no test to mutate here.

### ADR-12 — Consumer Audit of Record

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-09-02-12-consumer-audit-of-record.md`.
**Decision:** the set of real consumers is recorded rather than assumed, so
"who breaks if this changes" has an answer that does not depend on memory.

### ADR-13 — Storybook Web-Components Renderer

`docs/architecture/decisions/2026-09-02-13-storybook-web-components-builder.md`.
**Decision:** the catalogue renders through `@storybook/web-components`,
replacing the Angular renderer ADR-6 and ADR-7 reason about.

---

## 2a. Gates

CI runs these, and a component that passes only the obvious ones still fails.
The authoritative list, and the order to run them in, is
`docs/contributing/adding-a-component.md` §7 — kept there rather than duplicated
here, because a second copy drifts.

**Generators, all committed and all drift-checked:** `build-elements-css.mjs`,
`build-element-markup.mjs`, `build-react-wrappers.mjs`, plus
`nx run elements:analyze` for `custom-elements.json` (post-processed by
`normalise-manifest.mjs`, which also corrects two things the analyzer gets
wrong).

**Content and hygiene:** `check-manifest-content.mjs` (every public attribute and
method carries a description — `expected-docs.json` is an exact-equality
ratchet), `check-elements-entries.mjs`, `check-adopted-css-boundaries.mjs`,
`check-element-css-hygiene.mjs`, `check-no-css-in-source.mjs`,
`check-part-ratchet.mjs`, `typecheck-all.mjs`.

**Guarding the guards:** several gates ship a `--selftest` probe table, and
`check-gate-wiring.mjs` asserts the CI job still invokes them — a gate deleted
from the workflow is otherwise green.

---

## 3. Token system

All tokens are defined in `packages/tokens/src/tokens.css`. The generated
machine-readable catalogue is `packages/tokens/dist/token-catalogue.json`
(4 tokens, 13 categories, regenerated by `npx nx run tokens:catalogue` which
runs `scripts/generate-token-catalogue.js`). The Stylelint allowlist reads the
catalogue at lint time so the no-hardcoded-values rule is data-driven.

### Naming pattern

`--sk-<category>[-<modifier>[-<variant>]]`. Categories are enumerable; new
tokens must fit an existing category prefix or motivate a schema-level ADR
amendment.

### Colour (brand palette)

| Token | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--sk-color-yellow` | `#F5C518` | signature primary, CTAs, logo bow |
| `--sk-color-yellow-soft` | `#FFD84D` | hover / highlight |
| `--sk-color-yellow-deep` | `#C99A0E` | pressed / on-light foreground |
| `--sk-color-yellow-alpha-15` | `rgba(245, 197, 24, 0.14)` | hover accent |
| `--sk-color-yellow-alpha-35` | `rgba(245, 197, 24, 0.35)` | hover accent / glow |
| `--sk-color-yellow-alpha-60` | `rgba(245, 197, 24, 0.60)` | glow effects |
| `--sk-color-haygold` | `#D9B36A` | muted warm gold, bullet dots, dim accents |
| `--sk-color-haygold-soft` | `#E8C988` | softer gold |
| `--sk-color-blue` | `#A9C7E8` | soft icy blue (illustration sky / muted info) |
| `--sk-color-blue-deep` | `#6B8FB8` | hover state for blue |
| `--sk-color-blue-bg` | `#14202E` | deep blue surface for muted-info panel |
| `--sk-color-purple` | `#B8A9E0` | soft lavender, v2.x evolution accent |
| `--sk-color-purple-deep` | `#8C7AC2` | hover state for purple |

| `--sk-color-sage-deep` | `#3D7A3D` | hover / pressed sage, AND the light-mode `--sk-color-accent` (4.76:1 on cream, 5.19:1 on the card) |

### Typography — font families

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| `--sk-font-sans` | `ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif` |
| `--sk-font-display` | `'Falling Sky', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif` |
| `--sk-font-reference` | `'Swansea', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif` |
| `--sk-font-condensed` | `'Falling Sky Condensed', 'Falling Sky', ui-sans-serif, sans-serif` |
| `--sk-font-extended` | `'Falling Sky Extended', 'Falling Sky', ui-sans-serif, sans-serif` |
| `--sk-font-outline` | `'Falling Sky Outline', 'Falling Sky', ui-sans-serif, sans-serif` |
| `--sk-font-boldplus` | `'Falling Sky Boldplus', 'Falling Sky', ui-sans-serif, sans-serif` |
| `--sk-font-mono` | `'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace` |

JetBrains Mono is loaded via Google Fonts CDN. Falling Sky / Swansea ship in
`packages/tokens/fonts/` and are registered with `@font-face` rules at the
bottom of `tokens.css` (light + oblique cuts at weights 300–900 plus Boldplus,
Condensed, Extended, Outline cuts).

| `--sk-motion-ease-in-out` | `cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)` |

### Light-mode override pattern

Light mode is opt-in via `data-theme="light"` **on the document root** or the `.sk-light`
class on a wrapper element. The override block lives in `tokens.css` and
re-binds the surface, foreground, border, accent, tint, pill, and shadow
families. Brand palette values, the type scale, weights, spacing, radius, and
motion are *not* overridden — they are theme-agnostic.

```css
:root[data-theme="light"],
.sk-light {
  --sk-surface-page:        #F8F5EC;   /* warm cream */
  --sk-surface-card:        #FFFFFF;   /* lifted white */
  --sk-fg-default:          #1A1A14;   /* near-black ink */
  --sk-color-accent:        var(--sk-color-sage-deep);
  --sk-color-accent-fg:     #FFFFFF;
  /* ...full list re-binds: surface-{page|hero|card|input|pill|muted},
     fg-{default|body|muted|subtle|placeholder}, border-{default|strong},
     surface-tint-{mint|butter|lilac|sky}, on-tint-{mint|butter|lilac|sky},
     bg-pill, shadow-{card|elev|glow-primary|focus} */
}
```

The full block is at lines 183–228 of `packages/tokens/src/tokens.css`. The
sage-instead-of-yellow accent flip in light mode is intentional: yellow on cream
fails contrast.

---

## 4. Component manifest

Every component below has a Storybook entry. The catalogue's top-level
taxonomy is fixed: `Components/`, `Form/`, `Navigation/`, `Primitives/`,
`Tags/`, `Tokens/`. Stories render through `@storybook/web-components`
(ADR-13). A migrated component has an element story and, where it has a static
form, a styles-layer story rendered from the GENERATED markup — never
hand-written HTML in a story.

### elements package — `packages/elements/src/`

The custom elements. Each is a Lit element registered through the guarded
`define()` helper, with its CSS adopted as a constructed stylesheet generated
from `packages/styles`, and its static HTML generated from the element's own
markup module (ADR-10 §3).

| element | owns behaviour | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `sk-card` | no | `variant` (blue/purple), `inset`; default slot |
| `sk-nav-pill` | yes | fires `sk-nav-pill-toggle` with `detail: { open: boolean }`, cancelable; `isOpen` reflects as the `open` attribute |
| `sk-form-input` | yes | form-associated via `ElementInternals`; `errorMessage` is `state: true` and deliberately not a React prop |
| `sk-form-textarea` | yes | as `sk-form-input`, plus `rows` |
| `sk-grid` | no | `variant` (cols-2/3/4), `gap` (3/4/6); default slot; collapses to one column below 720px |
| `sk-section-banner` | no | `variant` (neutral/purple/green), defaulting to neutral on BOTH paths because the base class paints nothing; label is slotted |
| `sk-button` | no | `variant` (primary/secondary/ghost), `size` (sm), `href` (renders an anchor instead of a button), `disabled`; label slotted |
| `sk-check-bullet` | no | `icon` (the tick); sets `role="listitem"` on its host because a custom element inside a `<ul>` is not a list item; text slotted |
| `sk-feature-card` | no | `accent` (yellow/green/purple, the chip) and `variant` (border-*, the frame) — two independent axes; icon, title and body slotted |
| `sk-pill-tag` | no | `variant` (green/purple/breaking/yellow) and `shape` (eyebrow) as INDEPENDENT axes; label slotted |
| `sk-ribbon-card` | no | `ribbon` (label; the tab renders only when set), `accent` (tab colour), `variant` (border) over five shared colours; title and body slotted |
| `sk-stub` | no | zero public members; the deliberate empty case several gates are floored against |

Migration is complete apart from one component. #77 migrated `grid`, `section-banner` and
`site-footer`; #78 `feature-card`, `ribbon-card` and `blog-card`; #79 `button`, `pill-tag` and
`check-bullet`.

Two of those carry a design decision worth knowing. `blog-card` COMPOSES sk-card's stylesheet
(`static styles = [cardSheet, sheet]`, sk-card first) rather than nesting a real `<sk-card>` —
the first cross-component sheet adoption in the repo. `site-footer`'s content is entirely
SLOTTED, because a footer's words belong to the site rather than to the component; the trade is
that its element consumers must also load the stylesheet in their document, since `::slotted()`
cannot reach nested children.

**`form-field` is the only component still styles-only**, and it had no owning mission until
#141.


### react package — `packages/react/src/`

**Every file is generated** by `scripts/build-react-wrappers.mjs` from
`custom-elements.json`, and committed. Never hand-edited: `--check` regenerates
and fails on drift, on an orphaned file, and on a shrunken output set. One
wrapper per element with a `tagName`, plus `index`, plus `react-utils`.

Props are the element's public **attributed** fields — `state: true` properties
are excluded, because `ssrSafe` defers registration and React delivers
first-render props as attributes, so a property with no observed attribute could
never arrive. Event handlers are `on<PascalCase>` of the declared event name and
carry the detail generic from the element's `@fires {Type}`.

### styles package — `packages/styles/src/`

#### sk-button (styles)
- Path: `packages/styles/src/button/sk-button.css` (authored) + `sk-button.html` and `index.ts` (**generated** from `packages/elements/src/button/sk-button.markup.ts`) + `sk-button-html.stories.ts`
- Story title: `Components/Button (HTML)`
- Variants: `Default`, `Secondary`, `Ghost`, `Small`, `Disabled`, `AllVariants`, `LightMode`
- Notes: migrated in #79. The class family was RENAMED `.sk-btn*` -> `.sk-button*` under the #139 ruling, so the component's classes are prefixed with its own name and the ADR-9 ownership gate can verify it. `sk-button-primary.html` and `sk-button-secondary.html` are DELETED — the generated `sk-button.html` replaces them. Modifiers are `--primary`, `--secondary`, `--ghost` and `--sm` (not `--small`).

#### sk-card (styles)
- Path: `packages/styles/src/card/sk-card.css` + `sk-card.html` + `sk-card-html.stories.ts`
- Story title: `Components/Card`
- Variants: `Default`, `Blue`, `Purple`, `Inset`, `BlogCardExample`, `LightMode`
- Notes: surface-tinted card; `BlogCardExample` is the composition used on `blog-demo.html`.

#### sk-check-bullet (styles)
- Path: `packages/styles/src/check-bullet/sk-check-bullet.css` + `sk-check-bullet.html` + `sk-check-bullet-html.stories.ts`
- Story title: `Primitives/SkCheckBullet (HTML)`
- Variants: `Default`, `ListOfThree`, `LightMode`
- Notes: pure CSS (no JS).

#### sk-feature-card (styles)
- Path: `packages/styles/src/feature-card/sk-feature-card.css` (authored) + `sk-feature-card.html` and `index.ts` (**generated** from `packages/elements/src/feature-card/sk-feature-card.markup.ts`) + `sk-feature-card-html.stories.ts`
- Story title: `Components/SkFeatureCard (HTML)`
- Variants: `Default`, `GreenIcon`, `PurpleIcon`, `ColorizedBorders`, `Grid`, `LightMode`
- Notes: migrated in #78. `accent` (icon chip) and `variant` (card border) are INDEPENDENT axes; the generated constants show them independently, and any pairing is a story-level choice.

#### sk-form-field (styles)
- Path: `packages/styles/src/form-field/sk-form-field.css` + `sk-form-field.html` + per-state HTML files + `sk-form-field-html.stories.ts`
- Story title: `Form/FormField (HTML)`
- Variants: `FormInputDefault`, `FormInputFocus`, `FormInputError`, `FormInputDisabled`, `FormInputFilled`, `FormTextareaDefault`, `FormTextareaError`, `LightMode`
- Notes: state markup is split into separate `.html` snippets (e.g. `sk-form-input-error.html`) consumed by stories.

#### sk-nav-pill (styles)
- Path: `packages/styles/src/nav-pill/sk-nav-pill.css` + `sk-nav-pill-drawer.css` + `sk-nav-pill.html` + `sk-nav-pill.stories.ts`
- Story title: `Navigation/SkNavPill (HTML)`
- Variants: `Default`, `ActiveItem`, `Mobile`, `CollapsedStatic`, `LightMode`
- Notes: CSS only. The `sk-nav-pill.js` helper (`skToggleDrawer`) and its `.d.ts` were
  removed in #73 — `@spec-kitty/styles` now ships no JavaScript at all. Two CSS files: rail
  layout and the mobile drawer. The drawer arrangement is markup + CSS; the consumer supplies
  the toggle, or uses `<sk-nav-pill>` below, which supplies it.

#### sk-nav-pill (element)
- Path: `packages/elements/src/nav-pill/sk-nav-pill.ts` + `sk-nav-pill.stories.ts`
- Story title: `Elements/SkNavPill`
- Variants: `Default`, `Open`
- API: methods `open(invoker?)` / `close()` / `toggle(invoker?)`; state `isOpen`, reflected to
  the `open` attribute; event `sk-nav-pill-toggle` (fires BEFORE the change,
  `detail: { open: boolean }`, bubbles, composed, cancelable); parts `nav`, `items`,
  `hamburger`; one default slot for the items, authored once and presented as a row or a panel.
- Notes: Escape closes and returns focus to whatever control opened it.

#### sk-pill-tag (styles)
- Path: `packages/styles/src/pill-tag/sk-pill-tag.css` (authored) + `sk-pill-tag.html` and `index.ts` (**generated** from `packages/elements/src/pill-tag/sk-pill-tag.markup.ts`) + `sk-pill-tag.stories.ts`
- Story title: `Primitives/SkPillTag`
- Variants: `Default`, `Green`, `Purple`, `Breaking`, `Yellow`, `AllVariants`, `Eyebrow`, `LightMode`
- Notes: migrated in #79. `.sk-tag*` -> `.sk-pill-tag*` under the #139 ruling, and `.sk-eyebrow-pill` — a second component sharing this directory — became `.sk-pill-tag--eyebrow`, a SHAPE axis that composes with the colour variants. The builder functions `SkTagHTML()` and `SkEyebrowPillHTML()` and the `PillTagVariant` type are REMOVED; exports are constants. Tinted variants use the `--sk-on-tint-*` inks, not `--sk-color-*`, which is a WCAG AA fix.

#### sk-ribbon-card (styles)
- Path: `packages/styles/src/ribbon-card/sk-ribbon-card.css` (authored) + `sk-ribbon-card.html` and `index.ts` (**generated** from `packages/elements/src/ribbon-card/sk-ribbon-card.markup.ts`) + `sk-ribbon-card-html.stories.ts`
- Story title: `Components/SkRibbonCard (HTML)`
- Variants: `Default`, `WithRibbon`, `BorderYellow`, `BorderGreen`, `BorderPurple`, `AllBorders`, `LightMode`
- Notes: migrated in #78. `sk-ribbon-card-plain.html` and the hand-written `skRibbonCardHTML()` builder are DELETED — the ribbonless form is now the generated base export, `SkRibbonCardHTML` (formerly `SkRibbonCardDefaultHTML`). Border and ribbon colour are independent axes over the same five colours.

#### sk-section-banner (styles)
- Path: `packages/styles/src/section-banner/sk-section-banner.css` (authored) + `sk-section-banner.html` and `index.ts` (**generated** from `packages/elements/src/section-banner/sk-section-banner.markup.ts`) + `sk-section-banner-html.stories.ts`
- Story title: `Primitives/SkSectionBanner (HTML)`
- Variants: `Neutral`, `Purple`, `Green`, `LightMode`
- Notes: exports `SkSectionBannerHTML` (the base, identical to neutral), `SkSectionBannerNeutralHTML`, `SkSectionBannerPurpleHTML`, `SkSectionBannerGreenHTML`. The labels are placeholders — version strings live in the stories, not in the component (#77).

#### sk-site-footer (element)
- Path: `packages/elements/src/site-footer/sk-site-footer.ts` + `sk-site-footer.markup.ts`
- Styles: `packages/styles/src/site-footer/sk-site-footer.css`; `sk-site-footer.html` and
  `index.ts` are (**generated** from the markup module)
- Story titles: `Elements/SkSiteFooter` and `Components/SiteFooter (HTML)`
- Slots: `brand` (one element), default (one per link column), `legal`. The element authors NO
  text — not even the copyright year, which is why the generated placeholder reads `© YYYY`
  rather than a real one: a clock-derived byte would make the artifact stop matching a fresh
  generation on 1 January (ADR-11 item 9), and a pinned year would only move the staleness.
- Parts: `footer`, `grid`, `divider`, `legal`
- **Element consumers must also load the stylesheet in their document** —
  `@spec-kitty/styles/site-footer/sk-site-footer.css`. The content is slotted and `::slotted()`
  reaches only directly assigned children, so nested links are otherwise unstyled and fail
  contrast on the dark theme. This is the only component in the catalogue with that obligation.
- Variants: `Default`, `LightMode`
- Notes: marketing footer with brand mark, link columns, legal line.

#### sk-stub (styles)
- Path: `packages/styles/src/stub/sk-stub.css` + `sk-stub.html` + `sk-stub-html.stories.ts`
- Story title: `Primitives/SkStub (HTML)`
- Variants: `Default`, `Mobile`, `Desktop`
- Notes: styles side of the WP04 proof-of-concept primitive.

### Tokens stories

`apps/storybook/src/stories/tokens/` contains MDX/Stories rendering the token
catalogue (colour swatches, type ramp, spacing scale). They appear under the
`Tokens/` taxonomy. `apps/storybook/src/stories/getting-started.mdx` is the
catalogue's landing page.

## 5. Quality and tooling

### npm scripts (`package.json`)

| Script | Command |
|---|---|
| `quality:lint` | `nx run-many --target=lint --all` |
| `quality:stylelint` | `stylelint --allow-empty-input 'packages/**/*.css' 'packages/**/*.scss'` |
| `quality:htmlhint` | `htmlhint 'packages/**/*.html' 'apps/storybook/src/**/*.html' \|\| true` |
| `quality:commitlint` | `commitlint --from=HEAD~1` |
| `quality:all` | runs lint + stylelint + htmlhint sequentially |
| `tokens:catalogue` | `node scripts/generate-token-catalogue.js` |
| `security:lockfile-check` | `npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts` |

`bash scripts/npm-audit-gate.sh` is the FR-041 hard gate (high/critical CVE
fail). `bash scripts/check-action-pins.sh` enforces FR-043 (all GitHub
Actions `uses:` directives pinned to immutable commit SHAs).

### Nx targets

- `nx run-many -t lint` — ESLint across all projects.
- `nx run tokens:build` — builds the `@spec-kitty/tokens` package.
- `nx run tokens:catalogue` — regenerates `packages/tokens/dist/token-catalogue.json` from `tokens.css`. Run after adding or removing tokens; the Stylelint allowlist consumes this file.
- `nx run storybook:storybook:build` — produces `apps/storybook/storybook-static/` (NFR-003 budget: < 3 minutes; observed ~10 s on 10.x).
- `nx run storybook:storybook` — local dev server.

### Linting rules

- **Stylelint** (`stylelint.config.mjs`) — enforces token-only values via
  `stylelint-declaration-strict-value` for the `color`, `background`,
  `background-color`, `font-family`, `padding`, `margin`, `border-radius`
  property families. The allowlist is the token catalogue plus literals
  `transparent`, `inherit`, `initial`, `unset`, `none`, `currentColor`, `0`,
  and any `var(--sk-*)` reference. Class names must match
  `^sk-block(__element)?(--modifier)*` BEM, or `is-state` for JS state hooks.
  `packages/tokens/src/tokens.css` is the only file exempt from the
  no-hardcoded-values rule (it defines them).
- **ESLint** (`eslint.config.mjs`) — Nx flat-base plus
  `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` with the ADR-002 dependency direction baked
  in: `scope:styles` may only depend on `scope:tokens`; `scope:elements` on
  styles and tokens; `scope:react` on elements, styles and tokens; and a
  `scope:fixture` on any of those. Publishable packages cannot depend on
  internal-tagged libs. A project with no tag is not exempt from these rules —
  it is invisible to them, which reads the same from outside and is worse. `eslint-plugin-security` warns on
  object-injection / non-literal-fs and errors on unsafe-regex.
- **HTMLHint** (`.htmlhintrc`) — covers structural HTML quality on
  `packages/styles/src/**/*.html`, `apps/demo/**/*.html` and `audit/*.html`.
  Enforcing: the command carries no `|| true`.
- **commitlint** — extends `@commitlint/config-conventional`; the `scope-enum`
  rule restricts scopes to: `tokens`, `storybook`, `doctrine`, `ci`, `docs`,
  `release`, `deps`, `security`, `styles`, `elements` and `react`. Subject case must
  not be upper / pascal / start case.

### CI workflow — `.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml`

Triggered on PRs to `main`, pushes to `main`, and a nightly cron at `17 2 * * *`
for the security audit. Concurrency cancels in-progress runs per ref.

Job DAG:

```
changes  ──┬──> security ──┐
           ├──> workflow-pin-check ─┤
           ├──> lint-code ──────────┤
           └──> storybook-build ──> a11y ───────────┐
                                ├─> visual-regression ─┤
                                ├─> playwright ────────┤
                                └─> lighthouse (advisory; always passes)
                                                      │
              all hard gates feed into ──>            v
                                                    gate (FR-026 — blocks merge)
```

- `security` — `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, then `bash scripts/npm-audit-gate.sh` and lockfile drift check (FR-041, FR-042).
- `workflow-pin-check` — verifies every `uses:` is pinned to a SHA (FR-043).
- `lint-code` — Nx-affected ESLint, Stylelint, HTMLHint; commitlint on PRs (FR-017 / FR-018 / FR-019 / FR-020). Failures captured to `lint-reports` artifact and surfaced as a PR comment by the `lint-feedback` job for same-repo PRs.
- `storybook-build` — gated on `tokens` or `components` path changes (`components` includes `apps/demo/**` and `scripts/assemble-demo-dist.sh`); builds Storybook, uploads the `storybook-static` artifact for downstream jobs, and runs `scripts/assemble-demo-dist.sh`, which assembles the demo surface and fails if any asset reference does not resolve.
- `a11y` — runs `@axe-core` against the built Storybook for WCAG 2.1 AA (FR-021) using `scripts/run-axe-storybook.js`.
- `visual-regression` — Playwright runs `apps/storybook/src/tests/visual.spec.ts` (FR-024); diff artifacts uploaded on failure.
- `playwright` — cross-browser smoke `apps/storybook/src/tests/smoke.spec.ts` (FR-023), plus `apps/storybook/src/tests/nav-pill-behaviour.spec.ts`, which drives `<sk-nav-pill>` through the assembled demo page — the deployed artifact loading the real self-contained IIFE with no bundler, which is the path a contract test cannot cover.
- `lighthouse` — advisory only (`continue-on-error: true`), runs `lhci autorun` per `lighthouserc.cjs` (FR-022).
- `gate` — final job that aggregates required results; treats `skipped` (no component changes) as acceptable for storybook-build / a11y / visual / smoke but fails if any of security / workflow-pin / lint / storybook-build / a11y / visual / smoke explicitly failed. `storybook-build` is a dependency because it carries `[ENFORCED]` steps of its own; without it a failure there merely skipped the three downstream jobs, and skipped counts as acceptable.

Other workflows:

- `pr-preview.yml` — builds and links a Storybook preview per PR.
- `release.yml` — provenance-attested `npm publish` with SBOM artifact (FR-044, FR-045).
- `storybook-deploy.yml` — pushes the built catalogue + demo HTML to GitHub Pages.

---

## 6. Light/dark theming

- **Default** is dark mode. All token values applied at `:root` are the dark-
  mode set; no extra attribute is needed for the default look.
- **Light mode** on a WRAPPER uses `class="sk-light"`. `data-theme="light"` works only on the document root, because the token block anchors on `:root[data-theme="light"], .sk-light` and `:root` matches only `<html>` — on a wrapper it activates nothing (#93). (the
  `<html>` element for full-page light mode, or any container for scoped light
  mode). The `.sk-light` class is an equivalent escape hatch.
- The override block in `packages/tokens/src/tokens.css` re-binds surface,
  foreground, border, accent, tint, pill, and shadow tokens. Brand palette
  values, type scale, weights, spacing, radius, and motion are theme-agnostic
  and stay constant.
- The light-mode accent intentionally flips from yellow to sage
  (`--sk-color-accent: var(--sk-color-sage-deep)`, `--sk-color-accent-fg: #FFFFFF`)
  because yellow on cream fails contrast.
- **Storybook convention** — every component story exposes a `LightMode`
  named export. The convention is:

  ```ts
  export const LightMode: Story = {
    parameters: { backgrounds: { default: 'sk-light' } },
    render: () => `<div class="sk-light" style="background: var(--sk-surface-page); padding: var(--sk-space-7);">${SkComponentHTML}</div>`,
  };
  ```

  The `parameters.backgrounds.default: 'sk-light'` aligns the Storybook canvas
  background with the page surface so the component lands on cream rather than
  black.

- **ADR-3 semantic pairing rule** is theme-aware: each surface token has a
  matching foreground token (`--sk-surface-page` ↔ `--sk-on-page`,
  `--sk-surface-card` ↔ `--sk-fg-on-card`, `--sk-surface-tint-mint` ↔
  `--sk-on-tint-mint`, etc.). Mixing across pairs breaks WCAG 2.1 AA contrast
  guarantees in either theme. Agents generating UI must use paired tokens
  together; never substitute an arbitrary foreground colour onto a tinted
  surface.

---

## 7. Quick install snippets

### Tokens (CDN, zero build step)

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@spec-kitty/tokens/dist/tokens.css">
```

After the `<link>` is in place, every `--sk-*` custom property is available to
your CSS.

### Tokens (npm)

```bash
npm install @spec-kitty/tokens
```

```css
@import '@spec-kitty/tokens/dist/tokens.css';
```

### styles component (CDN-friendly)

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@spec-kitty/tokens/dist/tokens.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@spec-kitty/styles/src/button/sk-button-primary.css">
<button class="sk-button sk-button--primary">Click me</button>
```

`@spec-kitty/styles` ships **no JavaScript**. Behaviour lives in `@spec-kitty/elements` as
custom elements, designed to load from a single self-contained script with no bundler and no
import map.

**`@spec-kitty/elements` is not published yet.** `packages/elements/package.json` is
`"private": true` and `release.yml` publishes only `tokens` and `styles`; #80 owns the
release. There is deliberately no CDN URL here — an earlier revision of this section handed
consumers an install snippet for a file that had just been deleted, and replacing it with a
snippet for a package that does not exist would be the same mistake. The shape it will take:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@spec-kitty/tokens/dist/tokens.css">
<!-- once #80 publishes @spec-kitty/elements -->
<script src="…/@spec-kitty/elements/dist/elements.js"></script>

<sk-nav-pill label="Primary navigation">
  <a href="#" class="sk-nav-pill__item">Platform</a>
  <a href="#" class="sk-nav-pill__item">About</a>
</sk-nav-pill>
```

### React

```bash
npm install @spec-kitty/react @spec-kitty/elements @spec-kitty/tokens
```

```tsx
import { SkFormInput, type SkFormInputElement } from '@spec-kitty/react';

const ref = useRef<SkFormInputElement>(null);
<SkFormInput ref={ref} name="email" label="Email" required />;
```

The wrappers buy JSX prop typing and a typed ref. They are **not** required:
React 19 scores 16/16 on Custom Elements Everywhere for basic and advanced
interop, so the elements work directly. `docs/design-system/using-react.md`
records what the wrapper does and does not buy, measured.

`'use client'` is emitted for you and element registration is deferred into an
effect, because a custom element cannot run in a server render.
## 8. Adding to the design system (agent recipe)

Concise step-by-step that an LLM agent or contributor can follow to add a new
piece to the system without violating any gate.

1. **Choose a package.**
   - New design value (colour, spacing step, radius, shadow, motion curve) — `@spec-kitty/tokens`.
   - New component — the CSS source of record in `@spec-kitty/styles`, and the
     custom element in `@spec-kitty/elements`. There is no third choice: since
     ADR-8 the element is the component, and the static HTML is generated from it.
   - A framework wrapper — you do not write one. `@spec-kitty/react` is generated
     from the manifest, and a wrapper package exists only where a consumer needs
     one (ADR-8). Getting the element and its JSDoc right is the whole job.

   **Follow `docs/contributing/adding-a-component.md`** rather than this list —
   it is the maintained recipe and it names every gate you must pass.

2. **Create files** under the package:
   - `packages/<pkg>/src/<component>/<sk-name>.css` — styles.
   - `packages/elements/src/<component>/sk-<name>.markup.ts` — the AUTHORED markup.
     The `.html` and the styles-layer module are GENERATED from it (ADR-10 §3).
   - `packages/<pkg>/src/<component>/<sk-name>.stories.ts` — Storybook entry.
   - `packages/elements/src/<component>/sk-<name>.ts` — the element, registered through `define()`.
   - Update `packages/elements/src/index.ts` AND `src/elements.ts` — both distribution entries, or `check-elements-entries.mjs` fails.

3. **CSS rules.**
   - Use only `var(--sk-*)` references. No raw `#hex`, `rgb()`, `rem`, `px` literals on the property families enforced by Stylelint (`color`, `background`, `background-color`, `font-family`, `padding`, `margin`, `border-radius`). Allowed literal values: `transparent`, `inherit`, `initial`, `unset`, `none`, `currentColor`, `0`.
   - Add new token values to `packages/tokens/src/tokens.css` first, then run `npx nx run tokens:catalogue` so the catalogue and Stylelint allowlist update before the consuming component CSS is committed.

4. **Story file.**
   - `title:` must match the existing taxonomy: `Components/<Name>`, `Form/<Name>`, `Navigation/<Name>`, `Primitives/<Name>`, `Tags/<Name>`, or `Tokens/<Name>`. A migrated component has an element story and, where it has a static form, a styles-layer story rendered from the generated markup.
   - Required exports: `Default` plus a `LightMode` variant. The `LightMode` story wraps the rendered output in `<div class="sk-light" …>` — NOT `data-theme="light"`, which binds nothing on a wrapper because `:root` matches only `<html>` (#93).
   - Cover meaningful states: error, disabled, hover, focus — each as a separate named export, plus `LightMode`. Do not add
`Mobile`/`Desktop` unless the component is genuinely responsive.

5. **Naming.**
   - BEM with `sk-` block prefix: `sk-block`, `sk-block__element`, `sk-block--modifier`. JS state classes use the `is-` prefix (e.g. `is-active`).
   - Custom element tag names are kebab-case with the `sk-` prefix (e.g. `sk-nav-pill`), declared with an `@element` JSDoc.
   - Element class names: PascalCase matching the tag (e.g. `SkNavPill`). The generated React wrapper reuses that name.

6. **Run the local quality gates** before pushing:
   ```bash
   npm run quality:all
   npx nx run storybook:storybook:build
   ```

7. **Commit** using a conventional-commit message with a scope from the
   commitlint allowlist:

   ```
   feat(styles): add sk-modal primitive
   feat(elements): add sk-modal
   feat(tokens): add --sk-shadow-overlay token
   docs(docs): document sk-modal usage in storybook getting-started
   ```

   Subject case must be lowercase / sentence-case, never start-case.

8. **Open the PR.** CI will execute the workflow described in §5: lint, a11y
   (axe WCAG 2.1 AA), visual regression, cross-browser smoke. The `gate` job
   blocks merge until all hard gates are green. Lighthouse runs advisory.
   Lint-output is auto-commented on the PR if either ESLint or Stylelint
   failed.

9. **After merge.** `storybook-deploy.yml` rebuilds and pushes to GitHub
   Pages. If the change ships a token, a component, or a structural piece
   that consumers will install, bump the affected package version per the
   release workflow's conventional-commit-driven semver rules and let
   `release.yml` produce the provenance-attested npm publish + SBOM.

---
